answer: Admission is capped at 4 new identities per origin per day, which is the limit that makes bulk registration expensive rather than impossible. A farm therefore spreads across origins and pays for the distribution, while each origin still has to clear the voyage quota and the mirror admission check. Because the atlas audit records the origin of every admitted key, a cluster arriving through one uplink is visible after the fact. That is 19 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
